A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CodeSense, with the same benchmark framework and six research questions. Their full text, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 14 LLMs on code-semantic reasoning tasks, including benchmark accuracies and prompting analyses in Figures 3–16.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark evaluations and adds random-baseline results and an API-definition ablation in Tables 7 and 8.

M1.justification: The tracing framework, task construction, abstract-value mappings, and principal prompting procedures are retained. The added API-definition experiment is an evaluation control; neither version establishes a revision to the proposed framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Python, C, and Java project sources and semantic-reasoning tasks. The API-definition ablation uses existing function-call examples. The changed C-statement sample count affects sampling within retained coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds an evaluated random-mapping baseline for abstract-value prediction in Table 7. The 14-model roster in Table 3 remains unchanged. Gemini disappears from Figure 4's Python panel but remains in the corresponding appendix results.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes C-statement samples from 497 to 485 and total samples from 4,495 to 4,483, without explaining whether this reflects correction or resampling. V2 also introduces random-category selection and an API-definition control evaluated on 248 function-call examples. Existing metrics and inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.9 tests whether supplying API definitions improves function-call prediction. Appendices A.6 and A.8.3 add a chance-level comparison for abstract prediction. These are bounded additions to the retained code-size, statement-type, program-property, and prompting analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. V2's random-baseline scores and statements about insignificant improvements do not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 4 substantially revises Python statement accuracies: Gr-3.2's constant-prediction accuracy changes from approximately 0.35 to 0.93, altering its comparative profile. Table 7 adds random-baseline scores, and Table 8 adds API-definition outcomes, including Phi-4 accuracy of 0.125 without definitions versus 0.089 with them. Most other plots remain unchanged; the revised Figure 4 is not reconciled with retained appendix results.

T1.justification: The concrete-to-abstract mappings in Table 6 remain equivalent. V2 expands the informal explanation of code semantics but adds no mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs that change the theoretical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about a real-world fine-grained benchmark, an extensible tracing framework, three-language coverage, and LLM semantic-reasoning weaknesses. The new supporting arguments and controls do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds arguments about contamination resistance from generated execution values, language representativeness, and usefulness when execution is unavailable. Appendix A.9 attributes API failures to semantic-reasoning limitations rather than missing API knowledge. The explicit limitations in Appendix A.2 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 2.3 newly illustrates excluded trivial functions, including constant-return functions and redundant wrappers. Appendix A.4 describes adapting scripts, prompts, and debugger integrations to additional languages. These expand technical disclosure; hardware, inference configuration, tracing instructions, and resource links are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Valgrind paper, a Valgrind retrospective, and CodeScope, using them to support dynamic-value reasoning and benchmark motivation. It also expands discussion of previously cited execution-aware learning work. The principal positioning against other code benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose, the six research questions, and the main section sequence are retained. V2 expands task motivation and filtering explanations, adds appendix rationale and ablation sections, clarifies example questions, and changes citations from numerical to author-year formatting.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document template, title and author arrangement, heading styles, and figure, table, and prompt-box placement throughout. Figure 4's Python panel is redrawn with different colors, category ordering, and legend membership. Tables 7 and 8 are added, while existing appendix plots are redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: The random baseline and API-definition ablation add useful controls, and the expanded rationale clarifies applicability. However, v2 introduces unexplained disagreement between Figure 4 and retained Figures 9 and 11: Gr-3.2's Python constant accuracy is approximately 0.93 versus 0.35. Without a stated protocol distinction or correction explaining these results, the benefits and reduced empirical consistency do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
